messages:
lee: Kicking off perf validation for the new bos1 GPU cluster. Goal: kernel/driver sanity, NIC fine‑tuning, p50/p95 baseline for our gen2 models, and a clean handoff doc. Starting bootstrap now. Anyone can help with quick checks?

infra-bot: Deployment job `bos1-bootstrap-2026-03-18` started — nodes: 6xA10G, k8s:1.25, nv driver target:525.105.17. Logs: http://ci.internal/build/2234 :robot_face:

ana: I can join. Quick checklist I usually run:
- verify kernel module versions
- check nv_peer_mem / gpudirect status
- run small cudnn/cublas smoke and a synthetic throughput run

ana: Run these first on a node (copy/paste):
```
uname -a
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version|sriov'
lsmod | egrep 'nvidia|nv_peer_mem'
nvidia-smi topo --matrix
````

pradeep: Ran on node bos1-gpu-03: kernel `5.15.0-88-generic`, nvidia driver `525.105.17`, nv_peer_mem module not present by default. nvidia-smi topo shows `GPU0 NVLink GPU1` but NVSwitch absent (A10G config).

pradeep: Synthetic token throughput run (model: rwd-small-v2, batch=8, seq=512) with our perf-bench: `./perf-bench --model rwd-small-v2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --warm 20 --iter 200`
Output snippet:
```
mean latency: 45.2 ms
p50: 43.1 ms
p95: 88.3 ms
throughput: 356 tok/s
````

lee: p95 is ~88ms (higher than expected 60–70ms). Did we accidentally run with CPU affinity off or background IO? Check `iostat` and `dmesg` for any NV driver warnings.

pradeep: `dmesg` had repeated `NVRM: GPU fell off the bus` on boot earlier but only in first 2 minutes; no current errors. iostat idle looks fine. I/O spikes around kubelet startup.

ana: Check `nvidia-persistenced` status and MIG partitions if any. Also confirm `default cgroup driver` and `kubelet --eviction-hard` settings — I've seen misconfigured evictions add latency.

maya: Found kubelet using cgroupfs on two nodes; we standardised to systemd in main regions. That can change CPU isolation semantics. I can flip kubelet config and roll a node to test.

ops-oncall: Heads-up on capacity/cost — bos1 infra estimate after reserved pricing: $1,900/mo per A10G equivalent. If we need more P95 headroom we should evaluate moving some heavier load to dedicated pools or add 1 GPU per node and re-evaluate autoscaler cost thresholds.

lee: For kernel driver follow-ups: 1) enable `nv_peer_mem` if gpudirect required for our multi-gpu flows; 2) ensure `iommu=pt` isn't blocking DMA; 3) lock driver to 525.105.17 for parity with other regions.

ana: Quick action items I will run now:
- enable persistenced and nv_peer_mem (if kernel module available)
- run microbench: `python3 bench/latency_probe.py --gpu 0 --iters 1000`
- collect perf traces (flamegraphs) for the heavy tail

pradeep: After enabling persistenced and switching kubelet to systemd on bos1-gpu-03, reran perf-bench:
```
mean latency: 39.7 ms
p50: 37.9 ms
p95: 62.4 ms
throughput: 402 tok/s
````

lee: Great — that gets p95 into target range. Please add these exact commands and a short remediation section to the runbook.

maya: I'll draft the handoff stub in Confluence: BOS1 -> "bos1-performance-handoff" and include node list, kernel/driver pins, kubelet config diff, and the perf results you just posted.

ops-oncall: Also include budget note and an action to trigger sales/finops if steady-state usage crosses 70% of reserved capacity.

lee: Thanks — if nobody objects I’ll mark this thread and the runbook PR as the official handoff after maya's doc is up. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Job `perf-collect-bos1-2051209876` finished. Archived logs at http://ci.internal/artifacts/2234/perf.tar.gz

ana: ACK, will follow up with flamegraphs and a short checklist patch.

pradeep: Leaving a final note in the runbook about watch thresholds: set node p95 alert when single-node p95 > 75ms for 5m and cluster p95 > 70ms for 15m.

lee: Perfect — thanks team. Closing thread once docs + PR exist. :white_check_mark:
